newsitem.title: GERMANY: MG seeks deal with ex-CEO Schimmelbusch.
newsitem.headline: MG seeks deal with ex-CEO Schimmelbusch.

text.p: German industrial group Metallgesellschaft AG said on Friday that it would seek a settlement with its disgraced former chairman Heinz Schimmelbusch and its former finance director Meinhard Forster.

MG's supervisory board said it planned no severance pay for Schimmelbusch in the settlement deal and said the ex-chairman, who has been blamed for leading MG to the brink of bankruptcy in 1993, and Forster had accepted clear responsibility for the financial problems created at the group.
Schimmelbusch would receive 1.5 million marks outstanding from his period in office, MG said.
Metallgesellschaft went on to say in a statement that the settlement would end the dispute and that legal costs would be divided and that each party would pay its own costs.
"The supervisory board of MG sees the end of the pending legal proceedings as a damage limitation exercise. It allows MG to concentrate fully on its planned activities," the group said.

Schimmelbusch and Forster left MG after billions of marks of losses on risky oil deals in the United States were uncovered, forcing banks to step in and bail out the company with a 3.4 billion mark ($2.1 billion) rescue deal.
